description.narrative: GCDG will lead the full implementation cycle, including beneficiary identification, verification, distribution, monitoring, and reporting. The nomination base will be a pre-existing list of approximately 3,500 fishermen names obtained from the Syndicate of Palestinian Fishermen. During the inception phase, GCDG will verify this list at the household level, and then apply rigorous vulnerability-based selection criteria — including household size, presence of persons with disabilities, elderly household members, women-headed households, absence of alternative income sources, and level of dependence on humanitarian assistance — to identify the final 1,500 beneficiary households. Beneficiary lists will be cross-checked with the Food Security Sector (FSS) master list to prevent duplication. Oxfam will manage the direct financial transfers to the contracted retailers, ensuring compliance with requirements and fiduciary standards, while GCDG remains responsible for all field-level implementation and beneficiaryengagement. The voucher modality hasbeen selected because it preserves beneficiary choice and dignity, injects purchasing power directly into the local retail economy,and avoids the logistical complexity and market distortion risks of in-kind food distribution. Implementation will be supported by an operational Complaint and Feedback Mechanism (CFM) and two rounds of Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to verify beneficiary satisfaction, market functionality, and household-level food security outcomes.

participating-org.narrative: The Gaza Culture and Development Gr

The Gaza Culture and Development Group (GCDG) is a non-profit, non-governmental organization established in 1990 by a group of Palestinian intellectuals. Its primary mission is to promote cultural awareness across all segments of society and to contribute to sustainable development for a better future.
GCD GROUP Mission and Objectives: Cultural Awareness: GCDG focuses on enhancing cultural consciousness among Palestinians, aiming to preserve and promote the rich heritage of the region. Sustainable Development: The organization is dedicated to achieving sustainable development goals, striving for a future that balances social, economic, educational, and environmental well-being. Key Activities:Library Development: GCDG has been involved in developing libraries within government schools in the Gaza Strip. For instance, through specific projects, six libraries were established and equipped with trained librarians to support educational growth. Community Support: The organization works to improve social, economic, educational, and environmental conditions, aiming to uplift the community's overall quality of life.
Registration and Legal Status: GCDG is officially registered with the Palestinian authorities, ensuring compliance with local regulations and standards for non-governmental organizations.
